title: Existence of the abelian Čech augmentation quotient in one degree
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\iota$ a type, $U_i$ any family of open subsets of $X$, $F$ an abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and $q\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that for every injective resolution $I$ of $F$, the map $\alpha_I$ of [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction] is a quasi-isomorphism. There exists an additive map $c:\check H^q(U,F)\to H^q(X,F)$ satisfying IsAbelianCechComparison on every injective resolution, with the predicate defined in [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction]. This assertion has no normalization conclusion and does not require that the opens cover $X$.

source.place: Lemma 20.11.2, construction of H(beta) H(alpha) inverse and independence of the resolution

proof.text: Fix the chosen injective resolution I of F. Apply new-abelian-resolution-sections-iso to obtain the canonical section-homology isomorphism e with its Ext cocycle formula. The hypothesis hα makes H^q(alpha_I) invertible. Define c = H^q(beta_I), followed by the inverse of H^q(alpha_I), followed by e. This is a composite of additive morphisms.

For any other resolution J use Mathlib InjectiveResolution.homotopyEquiv J I, whose forward map lifts the identity. The global-section functor sends this homotopy equivalence to one, so its homology map s is invertible (Functor.mapHomotopyEquiv and HomotopyEquiv.toHomologyIso). Define t on total homology by applying the Cech functor, flipping and totalizing the resolution map. Prove alpha_J followed by the total map equals the sections map followed by alpha_I using restriction naturality and HomologicalComplex₂.ιTotal_map. Prove beta_J followed by the total map equals beta_I using the augmentation identity in degree zero. Taking homology gives H(alpha_J)t=sH(alpha_I) and H(beta_J)t=H(beta_I). The first equation and hα show t is invertible.

Given x,a,ha,z on J in IsAbelianCechComparison, transport z to the section cycles of I. Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right and cyclesMap_i show that its underlying section is the image of a composed with the resolution map. Apply the cocycle formula for e. InjectiveResolution.extMk_comp_mk₀ and the identity law on Ext show the Ext class is still J.extMk a. Hence c(x)=J.extMk a implies that this transported homology class is inverse H(alpha_I)(H(beta_I)(x)), by injectivity of e. Apply the augmentation squares and homologyπ_naturality to the proposed equation on J, then cancel the invertible t. This proves the equation for every supplied resolution and representative, without a covering assumption.

theorem exists_abelianCechComparison_core
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (hα : ∀ I : InjectiveResolution F, QuasiIso (abelianCechAlpha U I)) (q : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U q).obj F ⟶
      (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).obj F,
      IsAbelianCechComparison U F q c
